invariants.description: c follows the Tao 2011 steady state (Suppl. Eq. 91) from c(0) = 0: c = c_bar(Vm) (1 - exp(-t/tau_c)), using the module's own tau_c
tau_c equals Tao 2011 Suppl. Eq. 92 (ms) converted to seconds
hc follows the Tao 2011 steady state (Suppl. Eq. 93) from hc(0) = 0: hc = hc_bar(Vm) (1 - exp(-t/tau_hc)), using the module's own tau_hc
tau_hc equals Tao 2011 Suppl. Eq. 94 (ms) converted to seconds
i_Ca = 4*F**2*Vm*P_Ca/(R*T)*(Cai*np.exp(2*Vm*F/(R*T)) - Cao)/(np.exp(2*Vm*F/(R*T)) - 1)*c**2*hc (Tao 2011 Suppl.; the module's encoded form)

bc_sweep.rationale: clamp potential -90 to +30 mV (rest to action-potential peak of a sympathetic neuron); reversal potential +/-20 mV about the Tao value; conductances by 0.5-2; Cai 0.05-1 uM, Cao 1-5 mM (Belluzzi & Sacchi used 5 mM), T room to body temperature, R and F constant.

baseline.reason: candidates: the voltage-clamp steady-state and time-constant data of Belluzzi & Sacchi (J Physiol 1985 358:91 I_A; 1986 380:275 I_Na; 1988 397:127 I_KV; 1989 412:493 I_Ca; 1990 422:561 I_KCa), e.g. tau_hc 17.6-29.3 ms; set up after the unit/sign fixes.

calibrate.note: not_applicable: kinetic constants are hard-coded in the CellML; only the maximal conductance is a parameter.
